title: Separable extensions are filtered colimits of smooth algebras
statement:
Let $L/K$ be a separable extension of fields. Then $L$ is a filtered
colimit of finitely generated smooth $K$-algebras, and the colimit may be
taken over smooth $K$-subalgebras of $L$ with the inclusions as transition
maps; consequently $\Spec(L)$ is the inverse limit of the corresponding
affine smooth $K$-schemes with affine transition morphisms.
(*Source:* Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.158.11,
[Tag `07BV`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07BV); the
finitely generated case is the imported statement
[lem-kun-fg-separable-smooth] and the algebraic case is proved in this
chapter.)

proof.text: The finitely generated subextensions $L_j/K$ of $L$ form a directed system under inclusion (the subextension generated by two of them is finitely generated) whose union is $L$. Each $L_j/K$ is separable: every finitely generated subextension of $L_j$ is one of $L$, hence separably generated (Stacks, Tag 030R).

By [lem-kun-fg-separable-smooth] (whose hypothesis, a finitely generated separable extension, includes the finite ones), each $L_j$ is the directed union of its finitely generated smooth $K$-subalgebras.

source.place: ## Proof, classification of finitely generated subextensions

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S$ be the set of finitely generated smooth $K$-subalgebras of $L$, ordered by inclusion. It is directed and its union is $L$ (cofinality as in Tag 07BV: every finite subset of $L$ lies in a member of $\mathcal S$): given a finite $E\subset L$, let $L_j$ be the subfield generated by $E$; by the preceding step each element of $E$ lies in a smooth subalgebra of $L_j$, and since those subalgebras are directed, $E$ lies in a single one, which is in $\mathcal S$. Applied to $E$ a set of generators of $A\cup B$ for $A,B\in\mathcal S$ this gives directedness. Thus $L=\varinjlim_{A\in\mathcal S}A$ with inclusions as transition maps.

source.place: ## Proof, sentence on a filtered colimit of filtered colimits

proof.text: Applying [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] to the directed system $\mathcal S$ identifies $\Spec(L)$ with the inverse limit of the affine schemes $\Spec(A)$, $A\in\mathcal S$, which are smooth over $K$; each transition morphism is affine by the same node.
